images.title: One big step instead of three
images.purpose: Show that dividing 300 and 150 by 50 at once does the work of dividing by 2, 5 and 5, and gives the same HCF.
images.composition: A short two step ladder in the centre left and a small note on the right explaining the big divisor, with plenty of white space.
exact_structure: Ladder rows: 300 and 150, then 6 and 3, then 2 and 1. Exactly 3 rows, 6 numbers, in teal #0072B2.
Exactly 2 divisors to the left of rows 1 and 2: 50 in a large reddish purple #CC79A7 circle, then 3 in a small amber #E69F00 circle.
Thin grey #6B7280 division bars: one vertical bar right of the divisor column and one horizontal line under each of rows 1 and 2.
A thin grey arrow from the 50 circle to a note on the right: 50 = 2 × 5 × 5.
Under the note, one bold line: HCF = 50 × 3 = 150.
rejection: any row that is not the row above divided by its divisor
more or fewer than 2 divisors or 3 ladder rows
the pairs 90 and 150 or 84 and 132 appearing
images.takeaway: Any common factor can be used in one step; a bigger divisor just makes the ladder shorter.
images.description: A short ladder 300, 150 divided by 50 to 6, 3 and by 3 to 2, 1, with the note 50 = 2 × 5 × 5 and HCF = 150.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video on Guna and Anshu's faster way.
images.teaching_notes: Compare this two step ladder with a four step one in mind: the divisors still multiply to the same HCF.

image_decisions.why: A shortened ladder with the big divisor broken into its primes shows why the shortcut is allowed.
